title: Erdős #156 OQ-02: Maximal Sidon Set Lower Bound
description: Proves any maximal Sidon set A ⊆ {1,...,N} has size s satisfying 2N ≤ (s+1)³, giving s ≥ (2N)^{1/3} − 1 = Ω(N^{1/3}). Every non-member is blocked via sum collisions, and the blocking structure bounds the set size. 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős #156: what is the minimum size of a maximal Sidon set in {1,...,N}? A Sidon set has all pairwise sums distinct. Greedy produces maximal Sidon sets of size Θ(N^{1/3}). The upper bound Θ(N^{1/2}) follows from the Sidon condition directly.
overview.problemStatement: Prove: any maximal Sidon set A ⊆ {1,...,N} satisfies |A| ≥ (2N)^{1/3} − 1.
overview.proofStrategy: Maximality: every x ∉ A is blocked (adding x creates a sum collision). Collisions are type-1 (x+a=b+c) or type-2 (2x=b+c). Count blocked values ≤ |sumset(A)| · (|A|+1) = |A|(|A|+1)/2 · (|A|+1). Since N ≤ |sumset| · (|A|+1), the bound 2N ≤ (|A|+1)³ follows.
keyInsights: **Blocking lemma**: maximality of A means every non-member is blocked — it would create a sum collision if added.
**Sidon sumset size**: for a Sidon set, all pairwise sums a+b (a≤b) are distinct, so |{a+b : a,b ∈ A, a≤b}| = |A|(|A|+1)/2.
**Two collision types**: type-1 (x+a=b+c) and type-2 (2x=b+c). Together they bound the number of blocked non-members.
